system.name: AutoMan
system.one_liner: A workflow that combines automatic code generation with refinement-based formal verification to build correct, performant distributed systems.

content.subject: how a low-level execution trace's states map onto a high-level state machine's states under refinement

elements.name: H0
elements.role: first state of the high-level (abstract) state machine H

elements.name: H1
elements.role: high-level state reached after H0; the target of two low-level states' refinement mapping

elements.name: H2
elements.role: high-level state with no low-level state mapped directly onto it

elements.name: H3
elements.role: high-level state reached after H2; the target of three low-level states' refinement mapping

elements.name: H4
elements.role: final shown state of the high-level state machine H

elements.name: L0
elements.role: first state of the low-level (concrete) state machine L

elements.name: L2
elements.role: low-level state that also refines H1, making L1-to-L2 a stutter step

elements.name: L4
elements.role: low-level state that also refines H3, making L3-to-L4 a stutter step

elements.name: L5
elements.role: low-level state that also refines H3, making L4-to-L5 a stutter step

content.key_idea: A low-level state sequence L0..L6 and a high-level sequence H0..H4 run in parallel, with dashed arrows showing each L state's corresponding H state under refinement.
content.reading_order: Left to right along the top H-chain, then left to right along the bottom L-chain, tracing dashed arrows up to see refinement targets.

palette.used_for: all solid/dashed strokes, arrowheads, and text (state subscripts, 'Refines'/'Transition' labels)
fill of the low-level L-chain state nodes
fill of the high-level H-chain state nodes

style.stroke: ~1pt dark grey; solid for same-level Transition edges, dashed for cross-level Refines mapping edges
style.font: Times New Roman serif, bold italic for state labels (H_i / L_i), regular for edge-type legend text
style.arrows: thin solid arrowheads on same-level transitions; thin dashed arrowheads on cross-level refinement mappings

encoding.color_means: shade distinguishes abstraction level only: light grey (#f2f2f2) = high-level H states, darker grey (#d8d8d8) = low-level L states; the figure is otherwise monochrome
encoding.line_style_means: solid horizontal arrows are same-level Transition edges; dashed diagonal/vertical arrows are Refines mapping edges from an L state up to its corresponding H state
encoding.state_means: abstraction level is told apart by row (top = H, bottom = L) and by the slightly different grey fill, not by shape
encoding.marker_means: subscript indices (0-6 for L, 0-4 for H) give the temporal order within each chain; no circled numbers or check marks are used
encoding.emphasis: the uneven fan-in of dashed arrows into H1 (two sources) and H3 (three sources) visually emphasizes that several L transitions can collapse into zero or several H transitions
reusable_patterns: two parallel horizontal state chains at different abstraction levels linked by dashed many-to-one refinement arrows
weaknesses: no legend states the zero/one/several correspondence rule directly; it must be inferred by counting how many dashed arrows converge on each high-level state

evidence: a low-level state machine L refines a high-level state machine H
each of L's behaviors, a sequence of state transitions, corresponds to an equivalent behavior of H
Each transition in L (e.g., 𝐿0 →𝐿1) may correspond to zero, one, or several transitions in H.

summary: This monochrome diagram formalizes AutoMan's refinement-based verification approach with two parallel state-machine chains. A high-level chain H0 through H4 runs along the top and a finer-grained low-level chain L0 through L6 runs along the bottom, each connected left to right by solid Transition arrows. Dashed Refines arrows point upward from each L state to its corresponding H state: L0 to H0 and L6 to H4 each map one-to-one, L1 and L2 both map to H1 (so the L1-to-L2 transition corresponds to zero H transitions), and L3, L4, and L5 all map to H3 (so L2-to-L3 corresponds to several H transitions at once while L3-to-L4 and L4-to-L5 correspond to none). The figure visually grounds the paper's claim that low-level behavior can stutter or jump relative to the abstract specification it refines.
summary_zh: 图中两条平行状态链展示 AutoMan 的精化验证：上层 H0-H4，下层 L0-L6，虚线箭头标出每个低层状态对应的高层状态。有的一对一，有的多个低层状态映射到同一高层状态（对应零次高层迁移），有的一次跳过多个高层迁移。
notes: Kept prior 'logic' grouping and 'state-machine' base. No source-SVG colour histogram was provided for this figure, so the palette is taken from the measured index's top-3 fills (all grey, gray_frac 0.83). The exact fan-in pattern (L1,L2 to H1; L3,L4,L5 to H3; H2 with no direct mapping) was read off the rendered source SVG geometry, which the context text does not spell out numerically but which matches the caption's zero/one/several claim.
